tables.articles: Central article lifecycle hub. One row per article per revision per processing stage (PROOF = galley proof, EV = editorial verification, CE = copy editing). Every other table joins to this one. Tracks the complete workflow from submission intake through Nimble automated processing (nimble_start_time, nimble_status), IES human review (review_start → review_complete), support task escalation (support_task: open/close, support_start → support_complete), GRC abort events (is_grc_abort = 1 with grc_abort_reason/category), and final completion (is_completed = 1). The natural business key is (jid, aid, revision). Key filtering rules: use is_completed = 1 for fully processed articles; exclude is_grc_abort = 1 from throughput metrics unless the question is specifically about aborts; image tables join via articles.id (integer PK); error_logs joins via articles.aid + articles.jid (TEXT journal ID, not the integer PK).
tables.error_logs: Pipeline error log. One row per error event per article, recording failures in the automated processing pipeline. error_from names the step where processing broke down (e.g. IMAGEEXTRACTION, NIMBLE, GRAPHICSNORMALIZATION); error_to names the blocked downstream step. CRITICAL JOIN RULE: article_id stores articles.aid (journal article TEXT ID, NOT the integer articles.id) — always join on BOTH error_logs.article_id = articles.aid AND error_logs.jid = articles.jid to prevent cross-journal false matches. An article can have multiple error rows across retry attempts; use COUNT(DISTINCT article_id || '|' || jid) to count affected articles rather than COUNT(*). Presence in error_logs does not mean permanent failure — join to articles.is_completed to distinguish recovered vs stuck articles.
tables.images_init: Machine-extracted image baseline. One row per image per article, created when the submission is first processed by the extraction tool before any human review. Represents the raw automated output. article_id references articles.id (integer PK — NOT articles.aid). IMPORTANT: is_accepted is stored as TEXT — compare with quoted literals '1' (accepted) or '0' (rejected), never as unquoted integers. Join to images_update on image_id to compare before/after states and measure how much the reviewer changed relative to the automated extraction. Key diagnostic columns: rejection_category and rejection_reason for failed extractions; is_rasterize for vector-to-raster conversions; colour_input for colour mode distribution (RGB, CMYK, Grayscale).
tables.images_update: Post-review image state. One row per image per article, written by the IES reviewer and, for applicable customers, the MQC (Manual Quality Check) reviewer. Mirrors images_init structure but reflects the human-approved final state and adds MQC verdict columns. CRITICAL TYPE MISMATCH: is_accepted here is INTEGER (1 = accepted, 0 = rejected), whereas images_init.is_accepted is TEXT ('1'/'0') — never directly compare or UNION these columns. mqc_is_accepted and mqc_description record the final QC gate verdict (applies to ACS and Frontiers customers; NULL for others or images not yet QC'd — always filter IS NOT NULL before computing MQC metrics). is_support_image_replaced = 1 flags images that required specialist support intervention. article_id references articles.id (integer PK).
tables.profiler: Article intake and eligibility gatekeeper. One row per submission, created when the submission package is first analysed by the profiler tool — before images are extracted or any human review occurs. Determines GRC eligibility: next_process = 'imageextraction' (case-insensitive) marks articles eligible for automated processing; any other value signals manual routing, an error, or an ineligible format. MANDATORY FILTER: always apply is_active = 1 — inactive rows are withdrawn or superseded submissions that inflate all counts. submission_type classifies the layout: 'single_column' = eligible, 'double_column' = out of scope. Join to articles on (profiler.jid = articles.jid AND profiler.aid = articles.aid) — there is no declared foreign key; treat this as an assumed business-key join and include revision when revision-level accuracy is needed.
